# csvql

> csvql runs SQL directly on CSV files in place: read-only, no import, no database. A single Zig binary for macOS, Linux and Windows, usable as a CLI, a Python or Node library, and an MCP server for AI agents.

Use csvql when an agent or user needs to answer questions about CSV or TSV files (counts, totals, top N, group-bys, joins, schemas) without loading the file into context. Compared with DuckDB it is narrower but safer for agents: it can never write, `--root` confines file access to chosen directories, MCP results are capped at about 100 rows / 12 KB, and memory stays flat on large files.

Install: `brew install melihbirim/csvql/csvql`, `pip install csvql-query`, `npm install csvql-query`, or a binary from https://github.com/melihbirim/csvql/releases

Usage:

- `csvql --schema data.csv` shows columns, inferred types, row count and size
- `csvql "SELECT region, SUM(revenue) FROM 'sales.csv' GROUP BY region"` runs SQL; file paths are single-quoted
- `--json`, `--jsonl`, `--markdown` choose the output format; `-d '\t'` reads TSV
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 IO or internal error, 2 bad query, 3 data error under `--strict`
- `csvql install` registers the MCP server in Claude Code and Claude Desktop; `csvql --mcp --root /data` runs it manually with tools csv_query, csv_schema, csv_list
- Claude Code skill: `claude plugin marketplace add melihbirim/csvql` then `claude plugin install csvql@csvql`
